newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis pharma sales up 7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Novartis pharma sales up 7 pct in 1996.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals and chemicals group Novartis AG said 1996 pharmaceutical sales rose by seven percent for the year, with strong growth in the U.S., Germany, Spain and Brazil.
But growth in Japan was affected by government decreed price cuts, the group said in a statement.
Sales of its largest-selling drug Sandimmum/Neoral, indicated for transplantation and auto-immune disease, recorded growth of 10 percent.
Sales of the Lamisil drug, indicated for fungal nail and skin infections, rose by 50 percent, driven by a successful launch in the U.S., Novartis said.

Other growth products included Lescol, which recorded a 79 percent increase, the hypertension drug Cibacen/Lotensin with a 37 percent rise, osteoporosis medication Miacalcic at 30 percent and schizophrenia drug Leponex/Clozaril at 18 percent.
New cancer product Aredia posted a 94 percent sales rise and asthma drug Foradil sales increased by 136 percent, Novartis also said.

However, competition from generics had an appreciable impact on U.S. sales of anti-rheumatic Voltaren, which experienced an eight percent sales decline, and anti-hypertensive Lopresor sales, which fell by 27 percent, Novartis said.

Sales rose by two percent in the consumer health sector, which comprises the group's self-medication business. The segment recorded above-average sales in Europe where its Otrivin nasal decongestant and Rhinomer Nasal hygiene products reported substantial gains, Novartis said.
Generics sector sales were up 10 percent, due mainly to increased cephalosporin demand and a dynamic performance of the U.S. business, it added.

Ciba Vision sales were up five percent and agribusiness turnover rose by six percent in local currencies. Nutrition sector sales were up three percent in local currencies and specialty chemicals turnover advanced by three percent, also in local currencies, Novartis also said.
